channel.title: Upshot
channel.description: The week’s tech news, minus the noise.

item.title: Exploited: Drupal Warns of New Highly Critical Site Takeover Vulnerability Under Active Exploitation
item.description:
Drupal warned of a highly critical Drupal core site takeover flaw, CVE-2026-136716, that is being exploited in the wild.

  • Drupal warns that CVE-2026-136716, a highly critical Drupal core site takeover flaw, is being exploited in the wild.
  • Sites that left install.php remotely accessible after the CVE-2026-132165 fix may have been compromised, including production sites.
  • Update to Drupal 11.4.14, 11.3.23, or 10.6.23; Drupal 11.0.x to 11.2.x and 10.5.x and below are end-of-life with no fix.
  • Check logs for unauthorized access, verify user 1's email is under your control, and consider resetting its password.

item.title: Exploited: Mitel MiCollab Zero-Days Exploited in Suspected AI-Assisted Attacks
item.description:
Accenture says hackers exploited Mitel MiCollab zero-day flaws before Mitel's advisory, possibly with AI help, in an extortion campaign.

  • Threat actors exploited several Mitel MiCollab zero-days in a data theft campaign, according to Accenture; CISA added five flaws to KEV.
  • Attackers gained root privileges on a MiCollab server within half an hour, then reached internal backup and database servers.
  • Mitel has released patches for the five flaws, including CVE-2026-133275 and CVE-2026-133303.
  • Check MiCollab servers for indicators of compromise, since attackers may have compromised them before patches were installed.

item.title: Mock Service Worker Releases v3.0 with ESM-Only Build, Socket-Based Interception and GraphQL Subs
item.description:
Mock Service Worker 3.0 ships ESM-only, requires Node.js 22+, adds GraphQL subscriptions, and intercepts Node.js traffic at the TCP and TLS level.

  • Mock Service Worker v3.0 is ESM-only, drops Node.js v18 and v20 for v22, v24, and v26, and requires TypeScript 5.9 minimum.
  • Node.js interception moves down to TCP and TLS wraps, supporting socket protocols like SMTP; Nock also uses the Interceptors library.
  • Upgrading may break tests: v3 now intercepts browser OPTIONS preflight requests that v2 ignored. Read the 2.x to 3.x migration guide first.

item.title: .NET MAUI 11 Makes CoreCLR the Default Runtime and Adds Incremental XAML Hot Reload
item.description:
Microsoft's .NET 11 MAUI update makes CoreCLR the default runtime on all platforms, adds incremental XAML hot reload, and raises minimum Android and Apple versions.

  • Microsoft's .NET 11 release makes CoreCLR the default runtime for .NET MAUI, replacing Mono on all supported platforms.
  • Mobile and desktop apps share the runtime used by other .NET workloads; Android minimum API rises to 24 and x86 is dropped.
  • On iOS, Appearing now fires before a page is pushed; anyone relying on the old timing should switch to NavigatedTo.
  • Microsoft advises thorough testing of navigation, custom handlers and trimmed publishing; the Compatibility package no longer ships.

item.title: Exploited: CVE-2026-123903: Critical VMware Directory Service Authentication Bypass affects vCenter
item.description:
Broadcom patched CVE-2026-123903, a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated authentication bypass in vCenter's VMware Directory Service, in VMSA-2026-0011.

  • Broadcom released fixes for CVE-2026-123903, a critical 9.8 authentication bypass in vCenter's VMware Directory Service reachable over LDAP.
  • Unauthenticated attackers with network access to vmdir can gain access. A public proof-of-concept exists, validated by Rapid7, though no in-the-wild exploitation is reported.
  • Urgently update to vCenter 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0300, or 9.1.2, outside normal patch cycles. Broadcom lists no workaround and Quick Patch is not eligible.

What to do: Patch vCenter now; unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 bypass, following prior zero-day exploitation.

item.title: Exploited: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
item.description:
A Drupal vulnerability found by an Anthropic scanner is being exploited; CISA added it to its KEV catalog with a three-day federal patch deadline.

  • Drupal core flaw CVE-2026-132165, found by Anthropic's OSS Scanner, is being exploited in the wild for remote code execution.
  • The installer shipped with Drupal core lets unauthenticated attackers, under certain conditions, reinstall Drupal to hijack sites or run arbitrary code.
  • Upgrade to Drupal 11.4.13, 11.3.22 or 10.6.22; end-of-life branches get no fix. Also secure the installer after installation.

item.title: Exploited: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used to Root Firewalls
item.description:
A China-linked group chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia flaw in AI-assisted attacks on 25 servers; Palo Alto Networks has patched Fragnesia.

  • Palo Alto Networks released PAN-OS patches for Fragnesia, a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw tracked as CVE-2026-46300 and used to root firewalls.
  • Attackers chained the flaw with PHP2Shell against PAN-OS firewalls with management interfaces exposed to the internet.
  • Apply the fixed PAN-OS versions in the advisory, and block direct web access to management interfaces, allowing only the management network or VPN.

What to do: Patch PAN-OS and take management interfaces off the internet immediately.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
item.description:
Attackers exploited a CVSS 10.0 remote code execution flaw, present since 2016, to run OS commands on six Hex.pm package registry production servers.

  • Attackers ran OS commands on six Hex.pm production servers via CVE-2026-129514, a CVSS 10.0 flaw in the code since February 2016.
  • Packages show no changes, but attacker access to account data such as email addresses and password hashes cannot be ruled out.
  • All accounts were logged out; change passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and log back in to clients.
  • Until the new Hex client ships, fetch packages only from repo.hex.pm and avoid third-party mirrors.

item.title: Exploited: Drupal Fail2Install Exploit Details Emerge as Critical RCE Flaw Faces Active Exploitation
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-132165 (Fail2Install), a CVSS 9.8 remote code execution flaw in Drupal core, to its KEV catalog.

  • CISA added Drupal flaw CVE-2026-132165 (Fail2Install, CVSS 9.8) to its KEV catalog, with federal agencies told to apply fixes by November 27, 2026.
  • Unauthenticated remote code execution affects Drupal 8.9, 9, 10, and 11, and exploitation on live sites was reported as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC.
  • Update to Drupal 11.4.13, 11.3.22, or 10.6.22, the fixed versions the article lists.

What to do: Patch Drupal core now; CISA-listed KEV flaw under active exploitation.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploit Two GeoServer Flaws as Researchers Warn of Unauthenticated RCE Chains
item.description:
Threat actors are actively exploiting two newly patched GeoServer flaws, CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, per watchTowr.

  • Threat actors are actively exploiting two GeoServer flaws, CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243, according to watchTowr.
  • CVE-2026-120705 allows unauthenticated arbitrary file reads, while CVE-2026-129243 lets attackers invoke OWS operations that service security rules otherwise protect.
  • Eye Security reports the first flaw can be chained with two other GeoServer flaws for unauthenticated remote code execution.
  • Update GeoServer to 2.27.7, 2.28.6, or 3.0.2 as soon as possible.

item.title: Exploited: Palo Alto Networks warns of Fragnesia flaw exploited in PAN-OS attacks
item.description:
Threat actors are chaining PHP2Shell and Fragnesia exploits to attack Palo Alto Networks devices with internet-exposed management interfaces.

  • Palo Alto Networks warns attackers are chaining PHP2Shell and the Fragnesia flaw, CVE-2026-46300, to attack PAN-OS firewalls.
  • Exploitation involves PAN-OS devices with management interfaces exposed to the internet, which Palo Alto says goes against its best practices.
  • Apply the Fragnesia fixes for PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2, and restrict management access to trusted internal IP addresses.

item.title: Compromised: 1Password customer data stolen after employee GitHub account breach
item.description:
1Password disclosed a breach after an employee's GitHub account was hacked and used to deploy malicious code to backend services that stole customer data.

  • 1Password disclosed a breach in which an employee's compromised GitHub account was used to inject code that stole customer account records.
  • Customer vaults and their encryption keys were not compromised, but stolen names, emails and account metadata could be used in phishing campaigns.
  • Only a small number of users were affected and notified individually; 1Password found no evidence of account takeovers and is not forcing password changes.
  • Watch for unexpected invitations or recovery requests; use the 1Password website or app directly, never clicking email links.

item.title: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites
item.description:
The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy a constellation of one million satellites, roughly a 50-fold increase in satellites in orbit.

  • The FCC granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
  • The FCC declined a comprehensive environmental assessment, dismissing concerns about rocket launch emissions and satellite reentry pollution.
  • SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites and until November 2040 for the full constellation.
  • SpaceX must obtain a waiver before deploying Starmind satellites not disposed of via atmospheric reentry; the FCC did not grant that request.

item.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
item.description:
Rust 1.100.0 stabilises the never type and the core of the allocator API, makes Infallible an alias for it, and adds an opt-in Cargo dependency cooldown.

  • Rust 1.100.0 stabilises the never type (!) and makes std::convert::Infallible an alias for it, after ten years and five failed attempts.
  • Code on the 2015, 2018 and 2021 editions gets the never-type fallback change, so more code may be flagged as unreachable.
  • Upgrade issues: update dependencies first, since fixes for widely used crates are already published. Run rustup update stable.
  • Cargo adds opt-in global-min-publish-age under [registry] to hold back new crate versions; a beta tester found cargo install ignores it.

item.title: Australia passes tough legislation requiring big tech to preempt foreseeable harms
item.description:
Australia's Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, requiring online providers to set protocols protecting users from violence, rape threats and other foreseeable significant harms.

  • Australia's Parliament passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, opening possible billion-dollar fines for big tech firms failing to preempt online harms.
  • Platforms must assess risks annually in writing, curb harmful content, and add protections for users under 18 against pornography, suicide and eating disorders.
  • Users can opt out of algorithmic feeds, must prove age for porn, and major design changes like endless scrolling must be called out.

item.title: Migrating our Messages API to Rust
item.description:
Anthropic describes migrating its Messages API from Python to Rust.

  • Anthropic migrated its Messages API from Python to Rust, cutting CPU use per request about 70% and median time to first token about 20%.
  • Verification was the bottleneck: the production Python API served as the oracle, with shadowed traffic compared step by step.
  • Agents proposed fixes in sandboxed loops, engineers reviewed them before rollout, and the service never went offline.

item.title: AWS Lambda Doubles Its Timeout to 30 Minutes After Eight Years at 15
item.description:
AWS raised the maximum timeout for on-demand Lambda event functions from 15 to 30 minutes in all commercial regions, with no opt-in or pricing change.

  • AWS doubled the maximum timeout of on-demand Lambda functions from 15 to 30 minutes, in all commercial regions, at standard pricing with no opt-in.
  • Raise it per function with aws lambda update-function-configuration --timeout 1800, since Lambda rejects values above 1,800 seconds.
  • Check concurrency first: requests per second times average duration in seconds. A 30-minute run needs twice the concurrency of a 15-minute run.
  • Set SQS visibility timeouts to at least six times the function timeout yourself, because Lambda's check only runs when a new mapping is created.

item.title: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates
item.description:
Microsoft confirmed some customers face authentication problems after installing November security updates that fix a high-severity remote code execution flaw.

  • Microsoft confirmed November security updates for CVE-2026-118737 can cause authentication failures on patched Windows devices; no fix is yet available.
  • Affected are third-party authentication proxies, SSO solutions, and application packaging tools that do not correctly implement the NTLM protocol.
  • Long-term, update the affected product, use a Kerberos configuration if supported, or request a vendor update that complies with NTLM requirements.

item.title: DoorDash Scales Dispatch 10x While Maintaining 99.99% Peak Availability
item.description:
DoorDash redesigned its real-time dispatch platform into a distributed architecture separating coordination from computation, reporting 10x throughput and over 99.99% peak availability.

  • The redesign splits a stateful coordinator, which holds global logistics state, from stateless compute workers that run optimization and model inference over gRPC.
  • Before cutover, DoorDash duplicated production requests and logged the new platform's outputs against legacy assignments, so teams can shadow-test similarly.

item.title: GitHub Ditches CSS-in-JS for CSS Modules, Reports 55% Faster SSR After Three-Year Migration
item.description:
GitHub moved github.com from styled-components to CSS Modules over three years, reporting 55% faster server-side rendering and 25% faster component initialisation.

  • GitHub moved github.com off styled-components onto CSS Modules over three years, reporting 55% faster server-side rendering and 25% faster component initialisation.
  • The harder half was roughly 7,760 sx prop usages; a transitional @primer/styled-react package kept them working during the crossover.
  • Teams planning similar moves can start with the Primer React v38 release notes and the CSS variables migration guide.

item.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
item.description:
OpenAI says its GPT-6 models design protein structures and sequences, with lab tests finding binding across five targets.

  • In lab tests with Onava, 35 of 322 designed minibinders (10.9%) showed binding, with at least one binder for each of five targets.
  • Specialized models still supplied sequences and selected candidates, and predicting complete protein structures remains a clear weakness of the models.

item.title: Matrix Multiplication is Θ(n^2.25) [pdf]
item.description: An OpenAI-hosted preprint claims the matrix multiplication exponent is 9/4, giving Θ(n^2.25) complexity.

item.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
item.description:
WHMCS disclosed an unauthenticated SQL injection that can expose customer records and administrator password hashes, plus two flaws requiring a logged-in client.

  • WHMCS patched CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS 8.7), an SQL injection needing no login that exposes customer records and admin password hashes.
  • Logged-in clients can exploit CVE-2026-93700 (CVSS 9.0), an email campaign flaw that exposes database credentials and allows code execution on the server.
  • Self-hosted admins should upgrade to 9.0.10 or 8.13.8, or 9.1.2 on the 9.1 series; 8.0 to 8.12 installs need a fixed release.
  • For CVE-2026-93700, also delete all planned or ongoing email campaigns and empty the template cache, per the advisory.

item.title: Exploited: Check Point Security Management Servers Hacked in AI-Assisted Campaign
item.description:
Attackers compromised Check Point Security Management Servers in an AI-assisted campaign, launching attacks from 99 IP addresses against organizations in multiple industries and countries.

  • GreyNoise reports an AI-assisted campaign by threat actor GT13 targeting Check Point Security Management servers since early October, likely still ongoing.
  • At least 22 organizations in energy, engineering, financial services, government, manufacturing, mining, and transportation sectors across multiple countries were targeted.
  • The actor forged a signed admin session cookie to access an HFS server, then exfiltrated data from 24 compromised Check Point servers.

item.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
item.description:
Broadcom patched 23 VMware vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-123903, a CVSS 9.8 authentication bypass in the vCenter directory service (vmdir).

  • Broadcom patched 23 vulnerabilities across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer, including critical CVE-2026-123903, rated 9.8.
  • Attackers with network access to vCenter can bypass authentication through the VMware Directory Service (vmdir) flaw.
  • Fixed versions: vCenter 8.0 U3m; VCF or vSphere Foundation 9.1.2 (9.1.x) or 9.0.2.0300 (9.0.x); VCF 5.2.5 (5.x).
  • vCenter 7.0 fixes are available only through Broadcom Support for customers on extended support contracts.

item.title: Quad9 pulled their DNS service from France
item.description:
Quad9 announced it has deactivated its DNS resolver service for users in France.

  • Quad9 will stop all DNS resolution for French users on November 24, 2026, at 09:00 Paris time, after court-upheld beIn demands to block piracy-linked domains.
  • Any query reaching a Quad9 service address from France will be refused, affecting users who may not know of the withdrawal.
  • Quad9 says users should move to other resolvers, noting these lack its cybersecurity protection and may be less privacy-focused.

item.title: Interpreting a recent acceleration in pretraining loss
item.description:
METR analyzes OpenAI's published base-model log-perplexity for 13 models, finding pretraining loss has fallen about seven times faster since early 2026.

  • OpenAI published log-perplexity for 13 models since GPT-3.5, showing pretraining loss falling about seven times faster since early 2026 than in 2022–2025.
  • The data rests on one held-out corpus from OpenAI's codebase, and METR has no consensus on what it implies for capability forecasts.
  • Read the trend cautiously; METR says other held-out datasets, pretraining end dates, and compute and labor spending data would be most informative.

item.title: Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B
item.description:
PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, a 27-billion-parameter model using ternary weights, drawing strong Hacker News interest.

  • PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2.5 27B, an upgrade to Bonsai 2 27B with stronger agentic coding, multi-turn tool use, and multi-step task execution.
  • Built on Qwen3.8 27B with a 5.9 GB footprint, it targets developers building on-device agents that work with private files and tools.
  • Model weights are available now under Apache 2.0 and run on NVIDIA and Intel GPUs via llama.cpp or Apple devices via MLX.

item.title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated internet firewall mode (Preview)
item.description:
AWS Network Firewall adds an automated internet firewall mode in preview, applying central rules at each VPC's internet gateway with built-in NAT for outbound traffic.

  • AWS Network Firewall now offers automated internet firewall mode in Preview, inspecting traffic at each VPC's internet gateway with built-in NAT.
  • It affects VPC owners who route internet traffic through Network Firewall endpoints and NAT gateways, and it is available in all AWS commercial Regions.
  • Start in monitor mode with AWSManagedTemplateIGWFirewallBaseline in Network Security Manager, then switch to enforce after reviewing logs.
  • Before retiring a NAT gateway, update allow lists, because outbound source addresses change to firewall-assigned or IPAM pool addresses.

item.title: Introducing context-aware rules for AWS Network Firewall
item.description:
AWS Network Firewall adds context-aware rules that match traffic by VPC, subnet, security group, or transit gateway attachment rather than IP address.

  • AWS Network Firewall adds context-aware rules that match traffic by sending or receiving AWS resource, not IP address.
  • Rules track resources as they scale, are replaced, or move, so short-lived workloads like VPC-attached Lambda functions are covered.
  • Requires a transit gateway-attached firewall and a context store associated with that transit gateway in AWS Network Manager.
  • Create the NetworkFirewallContextStoreReadOnly IAM role in each account that owns a context store, then check the firewall's Context store sync state.

item.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
item.description:
OpenAI's Brian Yang described building the ChatGPT ads product with Codex agents and no human-written code, covering testing, sandboxes and batched reviews.

  • OpenAI engineer Brian Yang said a small team built ChatGPT Ads entirely with Codex, reaching $100 million annualised recurring revenue within six weeks.
  • Yang's core claim is that engineers now manage coding agents rather than writing line-by-line code, so the work shifts to building the system that builds the product.
  • Adopt gradually: automate one PR, then one feature, then one project, since jumping straight to project automation is where systems tend to break.
  • Gate agent changes behind unit, end-to-end and sandbox tests, and bundle 30 to 40 candidates for a day or two before human review.

item.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
item.description:
OpenAI detailed Pando, a backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads, reporting nearly 80% lower median push latency.

  • OpenAI has detailed Pando, a backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads while keeping familiar Git workflows.
  • Pando now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo, serving nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.
  • OpenAI reports nearly 80% lower median push latency, with Pando in production since April 2026.
  • Architects should weigh which consistency and transfer guarantees their workloads need, since multi-branch fetches lack a repository-wide snapshot.

item.title: Exploited: Azure Flaw Exploited to Target Secrets at Norwegian Energy Firms
item.description:
Microsoft closed an Azure API Management flaw that was exploited to steal secrets from Norwegian energy companies, with other sectors also affected.

  • An Azure API Management flaw appears linked to Norwegian energy firms' incidents, exposing secrets in APIM Classic instances.
  • Exposed data can include named values, identity provider client secrets, subscription keys and direct management API tokens. Only Classic tiers not following Microsoft's documented security guidance are affected; v2 tiers are not.
  • Norway's NSM advises treating secrets and named values as compromised, replacing them, and verifying instances are updated.

item.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
item.description: Z.ai announced GLM-5.4, described as its first loop transformer model, aimed at generalized coding tasks.

item.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn
item.description:
States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images and revenge porn, with state AGs saying it still makes CSAM despite X's screening claims.

  • Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX, alleging Grok still generates sexualized images of real people, including child sexual abuse images.
  • The states allege SpaceX misrepresented Grok's safeguards, which they say still fail to block non-consensual intimate imagery and child abuse images.
  • Affected parties include minors and women whose real photos were altered, plus X users who may have seen the images, per the states.
  • The states seek an injunction blocking SpaceX from operating Grok without industry-standard safeguards, plus civil penalties per violation.

item.title: VP ≠ VNP over Every Field
item.description:
A paper in Anthropic's formal-math repository claims to show VP is not equal to VNP over every field.

  • Paper claims VP is a proper subset of VNP over every field, via circuit size lower bounds for Hamiltonian cycle and permanent.
  • Both polynomials need more than m^(c (log m)^(1/3)) gates for large m, as do approximating circuits; the permanent result excludes characteristic 2.
  • Does not settle P vs NP. AI-written, with no human mathematician having checked the proof; the repository is unmaintained.
  • To verify, read Statement.lean against Appendix Q of paper.pdf, then run lake build and the Comparator script on Linux.

item.title: Ladybird Is Now in Alpha
item.description:
The Ladybird independent open-source browser project has reached its alpha stage.

  • Ladybird, a new browser with its own engine built from scratch, is now in alpha for macOS and Linux.
  • Expect some websites to break and occasional crashes, since the alpha ships rolling automatic updates.
  • Download it for macOS or Linux, and report broken sites or crashes from inside the browser.
  • Security testers are invited to hack it, but no security promises are made yet; report exploits so the team can harden it.

item.title: Kubernetes v1.38 Sneak Peek
item.description:
Kubernetes project previews planned deprecations, removals and changes for the upcoming v1.38 release.

  • Kubernetes v1.38, planned for December 16, 2026, drops kubectl WebSocket opt-out variables and makes kubelets require runtime-reported cgroup drivers.
  • Kubelets exit if runtimes cannot report a cgroup driver, and cgroupDriver config will be rejected. Upgrade older runtimes per v1.38 release notes.
  • On cgroup v2 LimitedSwap nodes, pods whose pod-level memory request equals limit get no swap. Check swap-dependent workloads before upgrading.
  • Remove KUBECTL_REMOTE_COMMAND_WEBSOCKETS and KUBECTL_PORT_FORWARD_WEBSOCKETS from scripts, and change kuberc allowlist name fields to command.

item.title: Introducing Claude Ship
item.description:
Anthropic announced Claude Ship, which can review pull requests, fix them, and approve those that a team's policy allows.

  • Claude Ship, now in beta, reviews, fixes, and makes approval decisions for GitHub pull requests on Claude Team and Enterprise plans.
  • Code Review is generally available; PR Steward and Claude Approvals are in beta. Zero Data Retention, HIPAA, and customer-managed key organizations are excluded.
  • Developers can update Claude Code and run /ship on a change. Admins turn on Code Review and PR Steward one repository at a time.
  • Run Claude Approvals in observe mode before requiring its approval in branch protection. Usage is billed on tokens, so set spend limits.

item.title: GPUI is getting its own repository
item.description: Zed's GPUI UI framework is moving out of the Zed editor repository into its own GitHub repository.

item.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
item.description:
Anthropic's experimental Code Mode lets Claude Code write JavaScript to chain, parallelize and filter Bash, Read and Edit calls, changing how auto mode and hooks review them.

  • Anthropic added experimental Code Mode to Claude Code, where the model writes JavaScript to drive Bash, Read, and Edit calls in one script.
  • Off by default; requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later and CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1, and works only in interactive native terminal sessions.
  • Hooks must check every part of a command; git push can reach one as cd 'app' && git push.
  • Project settings cannot enable it, so cloned repos cannot switch it on; admins can block it via managed settings.

item.title: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
item.description:
An analysis projects Anthropic's 2028 data center power mix at 87% gas and 11% coal, covering bring-your-own-power and grid supply.

  • Analysis estimates Anthropic's contracted U.S. data centers will draw about 87% of their power from gas and 11% from coal in 2028.
  • Emissions from Anthropic's power use could reach 17–38 million MtCO2e per year in 2028, with a mid-case of 32 million.
  • Anthropic has no direct U.S. renewable energy commitments, but has bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty gas generators.
  • About 80% of on-site gas capacity uses simple cycle turbines and engines, which emit more pollution per unit of electricity than combined cycle plants.

item.title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
item.description:
Google announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service running AI agents in isolated microVMs with checkpointing, keeping credentials outside the sandbox via an external gateway.

  • Google announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service running AI agents in isolated microVMs with checkpoint and restore, keeping credentials outside the sandbox.
  • Credentials, API keys and OAuth refresh tokens are injected by an external Agent Gateway, so agent sandboxes hold no exploitable secrets.
  • The service is not yet available and pricing is unannounced; Google is targeting a preview in the coming months, limited to Google Cloud.

item.title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
item.description:
AWS Lambda now runs GPU inference on EC2 G-series instances via Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU.

  • AWS Lambda Managed Instances now run GPU Event Functions on EC2 G-series instances, deployed as container images.
  • Up to 48 concurrent invocations share one model copy in GPU memory per environment, at EC2 On-Demand rates plus 9.75 percent.
  • Build an OCI image, configure AcceleratorConfig and a capacity provider, then publish a version; check GPU vCPU quota, since fresh accounts start at zero.
  • Only Event Functions are supported, so Web Functions cannot use GPUs yet; AWS has not said if that will change.

item.title: Exploited: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
item.description:
CISA added four flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation amid espionage attacks.

  • CISA added four flaws in Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver and VMware vCenter to its KEV catalog, citing active exploitation.
  • Attackers exploit CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller and CVE-2026-123890 in VMware vCenter, the latter linked to suspected China-nexus group Armory Castle.
  • Apply the vendor fixes; FCEB agencies are urged to patch all four flaws by November 23, 2026, under BOD 26-04.

item.title: Exploited: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
item.description:
Microsoft disclosed a breach in which attackers exploited a flaw in its Entra Connect Health service to access administrator email addresses and tenant configuration data.

  • Microsoft disclosed a breach in which attackers exploited a flaw in its Entra Connect Health API, exposing tenant metadata.
  • Exposed data includes administrator email addresses, tenant IDs, and sync status, but not passwords, tokens, or keys.
  • Microsoft deployed a server-side fix on November 19 and says no customer updates are required.
  • Watch for targeted phishing against exposed admin addresses, use phishing-resistant MFA on privileged accounts, and review audit and sign-in logs.

item.title: How Google Traced GKE API Timeouts to a Linux Kernel TCP Bug
item.description:
Google detailed how three interacting bugs in GKE, Private Service Connect, and the Linux kernel caused intermittent Kubernetes API timeouts that blocked about 800 developers from deploying.

  • Google traced intermittent GKE Kubernetes API timeouts for Private Service Connect users to three interacting bugs, blocking around 800 developers from deploying to production.
  • The Linux kernel bug discarded certain reordered FIN packets, leaving sockets stuck indefinitely in FIN_WAIT_2. The other causes were PSC packet reordering and Envoy's half-close behavior.
  • The kernel fix is a patch by Eric Dumazet, merged in Linux 6.9.7 and backported to the 6.6 and 6.1 LTS branches.
  • GKE customers receive the fix in version 1.33.5 and later.

item.title: Exploited: Chinese-nexus actor’s Cairn AI agents found a zero-day on their own
item.description:
Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a Chinese-nexus actor used autonomous AI agents, given the goal of obtaining shell access, that found and exploited a zero-day in an open-source application.

  • Amazon Threat Intelligence reports a Chinese-nexus actor's autonomous AI agents, run through open-source Cairn, found and exploited a zero-day in a medical imaging app.
  • The path traversal flaw in the application's upload endpoint let agents write files and obtain a reverse shell running as root.
  • The project's maintainers released a fix and a GitHub Security Advisory for the flaw.
  • Defenders should prioritize high-confidence detections that trigger automated response, since agent operations move faster than manual triage.

item.title: GitLab Critical Patch Release: 19.6.1, 19.5.8, 19.4.10
item.description:
GitLab released patched versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8 and 19.4.10 with security and bug fixes, urging all self-managed installations to upgrade immediately.

  • GitLab released critical patch versions 19.6.1, 19.5.8, and 19.4.10 on November 20, 2026, fixing security and bug issues.
  • CVE-2026-132825, a Ruby heap-based buffer overflow, affects self-managed GitLab CE/EE: all versions before 19.4.10, 19.5 before 19.5.8, 19.6 before 19.6.1.
  • Upgrade self-managed installs to 19.4.10, 19.5.8, or 19.6.1 immediately; self-compiled installs must rebuild Ruby with 3.3.14 or 3.4.13.
  • GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched and need no action.

item.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
item.description:
Anthropic closed its initial public offering of 1.127 billion Class A shares at $83.00 each, including the full underwriter option of 147 million shares.

  • Anthropic closed its initial public offering of 1,127,000,000 Class A shares at $83.00 per share, including the full underwriters' option, with gross proceeds of about $93.5 billion.
  • Anthropic received about $91.6 billion of the offering proceeds. Including a concurrent private placement of Class N shares to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA, and TSMC Partners, total gross proceeds were about $119.5 billion.
  • Class A stock began trading on Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19, 2026 under the symbol "ANT".
